head: 875edea
target: Document the plugin's distribution design: one shared tree installed into three harnesses, repo opt-in via a committed .own-your-diff marker instead of per-clone hook config, and how updates and Codex re-trust reach installs.
incidental: exact per-harness install and update command strings in the README
contributor check commands (scripts/selftest, claude plugin validate)
hooks locating the plugin root with dirname "$0" instead of CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which Droid replaces with a placeholder

questions.prompt: Why is a repo's opt-in a committed .own-your-diff marker rather than a per-clone core.hooksPath setting?

options.label: Git refuses to run pre-push hooks installed through core.hooksPath
The marker is what the pre-push hook reads at push time to decide whether to block
A tracked marker travels with every clone, so the session-start hook or quizgate sync installs the gate wherever the repo is cloned
A committed file lets each clone pin its own quizgate version

key_points: the marker makes opt-in a property of the repo: one commit and every clone of it is opted in, no per-machine setup
per-clone git config is machine-local state: it does not reach fresh clones, and an agent could flip it, which is why the guard treats core.hooksPath changes as bypassing the gate
the marker is read by the session-start hook and quizgate install/sync, never by the pre-push hook at push time

questions.prompt: A repo is opted in and a clone has the pre-push hook installed. Which of these hold?

options.label: A git push from a plain shell, with no agent or harness running, is still blocked without a passed quiz
Uninstalling the plugin from every harness removes the pre-push hook from that clone
The pre-push hook itself stops git push --no-verify
The session-start hook keeps quizgate current and reinstalls the pre-push hook when a clone is missing one

key_points: enforcement lives in git (.git/hooks/pre-push calling quizgate from PATH or ~/.local/bin), so it holds with no harness running and survives plugin uninstalls
--no-verify is handled one layer up: the harness guard denies it for agents, and skipping the gate is the human's call, never the git hook's
the session-start hook is the refresh and repair path: quizgate sync keeps the binary current and rewrites a missing hook

questions.prompt: A fourth harness arrives that reads the same .claude-plugin manifest and hooks shape. Where does its support go in this repo, and what stays untouched?
key_points: support is a thin adapter on the one shared tree: an installer function and case in install.sh (marketplace add, plugin install), plus a README table row
no copy of the skills, hooks, or manifest: the new harness reads the same .claude-plugin/ and hooks/hooks.json the other three read
only a harness-specific quirk like Codex's hook trust needs its own script, called from the installer
the gate path is untouched: marker, quizgate, and the pre-push hook depend on no harness
contributors bump version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json so existing installs pick the change up

questions.prompt: A contributor edits hooks/hooks.json and bumps the version, and existing installs pick up the update. What does a Codex install do with the plugin's hooks?

options.label: Blocks the session from starting until the hooks are re-approved
Skips the plugin hooks until the new hooks.json hash is trusted: rerun scripts/codex-trust-hooks or approve them in the Codex TUI
Re-trusts them automatically, because trust keys on the plugin version
Keeps running the old hooks until the new ones are trusted

key_points: Codex trust keys on the hooks.json definition hash, which the edit changed, so the hooks are untrusted
untrusted plugin hooks are skipped, not blocked: session-start and the guard simply do not run in Codex until re-trust
the version bump is the install cache key for Claude Code and Codex, a separate mechanism from Codex's trust hash
the git pre-push hook is unaffected: it is keyed to the repo marker, not the plugin version

questions.prompt: A new teammate clones an opted-in repo on a machine where no harness has the plugin installed, and never runs quizgate sync. They push unquizzed commits. Which of these hold?

options.label: The push is blocked, because the committed .own-your-diff file is enforced on the remote
The push succeeds: nothing on that machine has read the marker, so no pre-push hook was ever installed there
A single run of quizgate sync on that machine would have installed the pre-push hook and blocked the push
Their next session in any harness that has the plugin installs the gate for that clone

key_points: the marker gates nothing by itself: it is only read by local software, the session-start hook or quizgate install/sync
the design puts enforcement on clone machines and accepts this gap: a clone that never sees the plugin is unguarded
there is no remote-side enforcement; the ledger and the hook are local to a clone
the gate self-heals: sync or the next session with the plugin writes the hook
